flows.name: doc-audit-drift-interpretation-llm
flows.description: #362 (Moment 0 drift interpretation — narrow LLM judgment surface); cron-path invocation site corrected by #391. Per mapped drift event, the cron entry point `signals/drift_event.py::DriftEventSignalSource.commit()` delegates to the shared helper `routing/drift_moment0.py::route_drift_event()`, which invokes `drift_interpretation.interpret()` and routes the verdict. The library/CLI surface `helpers/handle_drift_events.py::process_events()` delegates to the same routing helper for operator replay (no longer the cron entry point). `interpret()` builds a cache-aware prompt and calls api.anthropic.com directly via the shared JudgmentClient (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). The verdict (PROPOSED_EDIT / JUDGMENT_REQUIRED / NO_CHANGE_NEEDED) plus confidence ∈ [0.0, 1.0] is parsed + validated against the E1 schema. PROPOSED_EDIT verdicts at confidence ≥0.80 feed drift_to_proposed_edit and onward through the existing tier_classification surface; lower confidence demotes to JUDGMENT_REQUIRED. Retry policy 30s/60s/120s; on exhaustion falls back to the pre-#362 issue path. Gated by [drift_interpretation].enabled in config.toml — flipping to false reverts to deterministic-only behavior in ≤60s (NFR-007).
flows.trigger: per drift event when [drift_interpretation].enabled = true in scripts/doc_audit/config.toml

path.description: Cron path (corrected by #391): DriftEventSignalSource.commit() delegates per-event Moment 0 + routing to route_drift_event(). Was previously routed via handle_drift_events.py inline.
Library/CLI replay path (post-#391): process_events() delegates to the same route_drift_event() helper so behavior matches the cron path bit-for-bit.
Per drift event, assembles DriftInterpretationContext (event metadata + diff + mapping rationale + current doc state for each doc_target) and calls interpret(client, context).
API key load via the shared JudgmentClient — not re-read per call; reused across the tick. Sensitive: never logged.

Single narrow judgment call per drift event. Cache-aware: system prompt (≥80% of tokens by char count) is marked cache_control=ephemeral per the existing tier_classification.py pattern (C-005). Returns strict JSON; defense-in-depth schema validation demotes malformed responses to JUDGMENT_REQUIRED (C-006).

Returns a DriftVerdict (E1). On retry exhaustion raises DriftInterpretationError which the caller (signals/drift_event.py on the cron path, or handle_drift_events.py on the replay path) catches → writes RETRY_EXHAUSTED ledger entry → files pre-#362 fallback [doc-audit] issue with diagnostic block (FR-008, FR-009).

After the verdict is routed (PROPOSED_EDIT through tier_classification, JUDGMENT_REQUIRED via [doc-audit] issue, NO_CHANGE_NEEDED auto-closed, or RETRY_EXHAUSTED escalated), routing/drift_moment0.py calls drift_ledger.append() with one AuditLedgerEntry (E3) capturing event_id, timestamp_utc, baseline, mapping_id, verdict, confidence, outcome ∈ {auto_committed, pr_filed, issue_filed, auto_closed, retry_exhausted}, doc_paths, retry_count, latency_ms, tier_classification_outcome, github_issue_number. Atomic append (tempfile + rename). The ledger backs the NFR-001 operator-triage-rate metric. Both the cron entry point (signals/drift_event.py) and the replay path (helpers/handle_drift_events.py) reach this write via the same routing helper.
